claims.text: A wheat-flour bakery; flour is handled openly throughout, so airborne and surface gluten cross-contact is unavoidable. No gluten-free production documented.
Breads and fillings include dairy, egg, meat, and seafood; no separation from animal ingredients is documented.
The kitchen is built around fermented foods and a body-friendly, health-conscious concept, so wholesome ingredients are a stated focus.
Okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside wheat batter and wheat-based noodles; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Hiroshima okonomiyaki sauce is wheat-based, and standard soy sauce contains wheat; no gluten-free sauce is indicated.
The single griddle is used for pork, egg, and bonito-finished dishes, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.

name: カフェ レンテ (Cafe Lente)

claims.text: 赤米とほうれん草の豆乳リゾットはグルテンフリーで、ベジタリアン・ヴィーガンの人でも食べられると複数媒体で紹介されている。
野菜をたっぷり使った健康志向のメニューで、外国人観光客にも人気と記載されている。

name: ちんちくりん 薬研堀本店 (Chinchikurin Yagenbori Honten)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is assembled and cooked on a shared teppan griddle where wheat batter and wheat noodles are cooked alongside all other dishes; no separate gluten-free preparation is documented.
Dishes are finished with Otafuku okonomiyaki sauce, which is wheat-containing.
All dishes are cooked on a shared teppan used for pork, beef, seafood, and egg; no vegan preparation area is documented.

name: 中国料理 川菜味 (Chugoku Ryori Kawanami)

claims.text: The brothless tantanmen is described as having a soy-sauce-based seasoning, and Japanese soy sauce is typically brewed with wheat.

name: 中華そば 千番 流川店 (Chuka Soba Senban Nagarekawa-ten)

claims.text: The signature broth is soy-sauce-based, and Japanese soy sauce normally contains wheat; the noodles are also wheat.
Broth is a pork-bone (tonkotsu) and soy stock and many dishes contain pork, so vegan diners cannot be accommodated.

name: 中華そば 陽気 江波本店 (Chuka Soba Yoki (Eba Honten))

claims.text: The kitchen prepares wheat ramen noodles as its only product, so any gluten-free request would face heavy cross-contact in a shared noodle-cooking environment.
Soy sauce is described as the key ingredient of the soup, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
The broth is a pork-bone and soy-sauce base and the dish is topped with char siu pork, so animal products are central to every bowl.
